justice: The wide, flat separated path on the right improves accessibility for wheelchair users, reflecting inclusive physical design
The complete lack of tactile paving on the side path reduces fairness for visually impaired individuals
The allocation of a dedicated non-motorized lane protected by bollards demonstrates equitable space distribution among drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists
safety: Sturdy bollards on the right strictly separate motor vehicles from the active travel path, protecting older adults, teenagers, and cyclists
Metal guardrails on the left prevent vehicles from veering into the waterfront green space, ensuring driver safety
Solar streetlights equipped with panels ensure continuous lighting, enhancing nighttime visibility and safety for all road users
livability: The total absence of commercial frontages or shops fails to support the daily convenience needs of residents and older adults
The adjacent waterfront and expansive green lawn provide a high-quality leisure and recreational environment suitable for all social groups
The lack of street activity, pedestrians, and residential buildings reduces 'eyes on the street', potentially impacting perceived security for adolescents
sustainability: Solar panels mounted on every streetlight actively utilize renewable energy, promoting low-carbon infrastructure
Continuous rows of trees and grass buffers on both sides provide significant green infrastructure and ecological benefits
The dedicated side lane protected by bollards encourages sustainable, non-motorized travel for cyclists and pedestrians
aesthetics: The unobstructed view of the water body and distant city skyline provides a visually appealing landscape for all road users
The uniform spacing of solar streetlights and roadside trees creates a strong sense of visual order and architectural rhythm
The clean, well-maintained asphalt road surface without visible litter enhances the overall visual quality of the streetscape
comfort: The lack of benches or resting facilities along the path significantly reduces physical comfort for older adults needing frequent breaks
Roadside trees on the right offer some canopy shade, though limited on the main road, aiding thermal comfort for pedestrians and cyclists
The wide open spatial layout and proximity to water reduce feelings of crowding, providing high psychological comfort for all social groups
walkability: The dedicated right-side path separated by bollards offers a continuous and safe walking route free from motor vehicle interference
The absence of tactile paving on the walking surface creates severe navigational barriers for visually impaired pedestrians
The lack of visible crosswalks or pedestrian intersections in this stretch restricts route connectivity to the waterfront side
bikeability: The wide side lane separated by bollards provides a highly secure and dedicated right-of-way for cyclists of all ages
The smooth asphalt paving on the non-motorized lane minimizes rolling resistance, enhancing physical comfort during cycling
The absence of clear painted bike lane markings within the side path may lead to right-of-way conflicts between cyclists and pedestrians
